body:
![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

In the `trap` block, `New-Item` and `Set-Content` are executed before printing the error to the console. If the `$WorkRoot` directory cannot be created (for example, if the `R:` drive is not mounted or there are permission issues), these commands will throw a terminating error because `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'`. This will prevent `[Console]::Error.WriteLine($text)` from executing, completely masking the original error that triggered the trap.

To fix this, print the error to the console first, and wrap the file system operations in a `try/catch` block to ensure they fail gracefully without suppressing the original error output. Additionally, avoid using the `exit` command to signal failures if this script is executed in interactive sessions, as it terminates the entire PowerShell host process. Use `throw` instead to preserve failure semantics without terminating the interactive host.

```
trap {
    $record = $_ | Format-List * -Force | Out-String
    $text = "Golden image build failed at $([DateTime]::UtcNow.ToString('o'))" + [Environment]::NewLine + $record
    [Console]::Error.WriteLine($text)
    try {
        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $WorkRoot -Force | Out-Null
        Set-Content -LiteralPath $failureLog -Value $text -Encoding UTF8
    } catch {
        [Console]::Error.WriteLine("Failed to write failure log to $failureLog: $_")
    }
    throw $_
}
```

</details>

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Write the original failure before touching WorkRoot**

When a preflight failure happens because the runner pool drive is unavailable or `-WorkRoot` is invalid/unwritable, the trap now calls `New-Item` on that same path before writing anything to stderr. With `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'`, that secondary failure can abort the trap and mask the original host/storage assertion, so diagnostics are still lost in exactly the missing-work-root case this change is meant to surface; make file logging best-effort or emit stderr before creating the directory.
